finding_dispositions.note: All four parts (a)-(d) were applied to research/interpretations.md, with the superseded statements explicitly withdrawn. No retrieval or evidence change was needed. The quoted Hilary and Chrysostom loci were re-verified against the tracked or recorded deliveries.

summary: Re-entered research for STU-020 and brought research/interpretations.md into line with the study as reviewed. No new retrieval and no change of evidence: Hilary In Matth. VIII §§ 7-8 was re-checked in the tracked PL 9 layer (SHA-256 db389fea...ada51 matched), and the section numbers of Chrysostom's Hom. in 1 Cor. 2 in the NPNF delivery (SHA-256 66bffe29...5858 matched scope § 6.3) were re-checked. (a) § 3.2 now records Hilary VIII § 8 (PL 9, cols. 961-962) as a witness of the third reading at Mt 9:8, with its wording and note (f). Its join of the Gospel's end to the Epistle's opening is labelled editorial synthesis, and the § 3.3 gospel row carries the same. (b) § 4.3 withdraws, and says it withdraws, 'All three treat ... the same way', 'a study that staged that contest would be inventing it' and 'none of the three readings turns on it'. It now states that the first reading does not use v. 8; that the second reports Chrysostom first and Hilary after, takes its own sense from Schuster, and cites Hilary only to show that the men of the verse receive forgiveness rather than minister it; and that the third takes Hilary's side. The Chrysostom-Hilary difference is recorded as the one disagreement that runs between two readings, and §§ 2.2, 2.5, 3.6, 4.2 and 4.5 are aligned with this. § 1.3's gospel row no longer gives the first reading the crowd's praise. (c) § 2.4 Anagogical now rests on Hilary VIII § 7, Ambrose V.14 and Aquinas's domus aeternitatis, and § 2.2 gains the Hilary § 7 witness. § 3.4 Anagogical rests on 1 Cor 1:8 (the confirming is Christ's on either reading) and perficias, both stated as the third reading's anchors only. The § 2.3 epistle and postcommunion rows and § 4.4's overview no longer lend those anchors to the second reading. (d) Chrysostom's 'not only the beginnings must be good, but the end also' and 'need of many labors' now stand only at 1 Cor 1:7 (§ 6), in §§ 3.2, 3.5 and 4.5. His reading of v. 8 is given only as covert accusation (§ 7). Both have been removed from § 2.3 and § 3.4. Also aligned with the study: the § 2.3 gradual and alleluia rows, and § 2.4 Allegorical. Ambrose V.15 is recorded as judging the fear more severely than Chrysostom and identifying the fearers with the calumniators. check-proper-components --phase scope passes. Remaining limitations: no other research record changed. The study's own sentences named in advisories STU-021 and STU-022 are study-owned and were not touched. Research review must now confirm the record against the study.
